chunks: Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is the restricted (physically) man and the restricted woman repudiated from the marriage?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

Rifa'ah said: 'And I asked him about the vitiligo woman. So he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a woman whose guardian married her off and she was vitiligo, that she has the dower for what she permitted of her private part, and that the dower is upon the one who married her off; and the dower came to be upon him because he deceived her. And if a man married a woman and a man who married her off did not know the interior of her matter, there would not be anything upon him, and the dower would be taken from her'.

key_terms.دَخِيلَةَ أَمْرِهَا: The interior of her matter (her specific condition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage for a person with vitiligo or physical restriction, and who bears the dower if the condition was concealed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that physical conditions like vitiligo (barṣāʾ) do not invalidate marriage, distinguishing between the spouse's right to the dower and the guardian's liability for deception (*dalās*). It highlights the Shia legal principle that if a guardian conceals a defect, they bear the financial responsibility, whereas a guardian unaware of the condition incurs no penalty, emphasizing transparency in marital contracts. This ruling underscores the importance of *kafāʾah* (compatibility) and the protection of the wife's rights against hidden defects in the context of Imami jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Rafa’at Bin Musa who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The (physically) restricted man and the (physically) restricted woman, would they be repudiated from the marriage?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

Rafa’at (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the ones with vitiligo. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a woman whose guardian got her married and she was with vitiligo that, there shall be a dower for her due to what she had permitted from her private parts, and that the dower is upon the one who got her married; but rather, the dower came to be upon him because he had cheated with her, and had a man married a woman and a man who had got her married off did not know the interior of her matter, there would not be anything upon him, and the dower would be taken back from her’.
en.sarwar: 9. Sahl has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Rifa’ah who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who suffers from al-Bars (albino).

He (the Imam) said, ‘’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, issued a judgment, in the case of a woman who was given in marriage by her guardian when she suffered from al-Bars, that she deserves mahr (dower) which must be paid by the one who gave her in marriage. Mahr (dower) is on him because he cheated. If a man marries a woman and a man who does not know about her cheating gives her in marriage he does not owe anything but she must return the mahr (dower) back.’”
